topic: How Transformers Remember: MLPs as Key-Value Memories
target_audience: University students and AI enthusiasts with basic knowledge of neural networks

outline.topic: How Transformers Remember: MLPs as Key-Value Memories
outline.target_audience: University students and AI enthusiasts with basic knowledge of neural networks

sections.title: The Mystery of AI Memory
sections.content: Introduce the concept that while Attention layers help Transformers 'understand' context, the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) layers act as the 'long-term memory' or the 'fact database' of the model. Use the analogy of a librarian vs. the books.
sections.example: When you ask 'What is the capital of France?', Attention looks at the relationship between 'Capital' and 'France', but the MLP actually retrieves the word 'Paris'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Dot Product as a Similarity Search
sections.content: Explain the mathematical prerequisite: The dot product. Visually represent two vectors as arrows. When arrows point in the same direction, the value is high (a 'hit'). This is how the model 'recognizes' a specific concept.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'France' vector and a 'Pattern' vector. If they align, a specific neuron 'fires' to say 'I recognize this fact!'

sections.title: The MLP Architecture: The 'Sandwich' Structure
sections.content: Break down the MLP into two stages: 1. Expansion (Key detection) and 2. Projection (Value retrieval). Show the math as a two-step matrix multiplication: Hidden = f(X * W1) then Output = Hidden * W2.
sections.example: Think of W1 as a wall of 4,000 light bulbs. If you mention 'Eiffel Tower', light bulb #742 turns on because it recognizes that specific pattern.

sections.title: The Key-Value Memory Mechanism
sections.content: Deep dive into the theory that each neuron in the hidden layer corresponds to a 'Key' (in W1) and a 'Value' (in W2). The Key is the pattern (e.g., 'The capital of [Country]') and the Value is the information to add (e.g., '[City Name]').
sections.example: A diagram showing the 'Key' vector matching 'Mount Everest' and the corresponding 'Value' vector injecting the concept of 'Himalayas' into the model's processing stream.

sections.title: Step-by-Step: Extracting a Fact
sections.content: Walk through a visual flow of a single token passing through an MLP. 1. Token vector enters. 2. It hits a 'Knowledge Neuron'. 3. The activation function (ReLU/GeLU) filters out noise. 4. The 'Value' vector is added to the token's representation.
sections.example: Input: 'Elon Musk'. Hidden Layer Neuron #1024 activates (The 'CEO of Tesla' neuron). Output: The vector for 'Elon Musk' is now enriched with 'SpaceX' and 'Tesla' information.

sections.title: Summary and Scaling
sections.content: Summarize that with billions of parameters, the model has millions of these tiny Key-Value pairs stored. Conclude with how this makes the Transformer a massive, searchable lookup table with 'soft' logic.
sections.example: Just as a massive library uses an index (W1) to find a page (W2), the Transformer uses MLPs to index the world's knowledge.

storyboard.title: The Mystery of AI Memory
lecture_lines: Transformers use attention for context and MLPs for memory.
Attention is like a librarian finding relevant books.
MLP layers store the actual facts and information.
animations: Show 'Attention' (blue) and 'MLP' (green) blocks in a Transformer.
Animate a 'Librarian' icon next to Attention and 'Books' next to MLP.
Question 'Capital of France?' enters; Attention highlights 'Capital' and 'France'; MLP glows.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Dot Product as a Similarity Search
lecture_lines: The dot product measures similarity between two vectors.
Aligned vectors produce a high positive score.
High scores signal that the model recognizes a concept.
animations: Draw two vectors as white arrows in a dark 2D space.
Rotate vectors until they align; show a 'Similarity' bar filling with #00FF00.
Label vectors 'France' and 'Pattern'; pulse the 'Similarity' bar on alignment.

storyboard.title: The MLP Architecture: The 'Sandwich' Structure
lecture_lines: MLPs use a two-step matrix multiplication process.
First, the expansion layer detects specific patterns.
Think of these as thousands of specialized light bulbs.
If a pattern matches, the corresponding neuron fires.
Then, the projection layer retrieves the associated information.
animations: Show input vector X entering a matrix W1 (#FFD700), expanding to a wider layer.
Visualize the wide layer as a grid of 4,000 dim circles.
One circle (#742) turns bright yellow (#FFFF00) as 'Eiffel Tower' is shown.
Highlight the activated neuron #742 with a pulsing glow effect.
Show the wide layer multiplying by matrix W2 (#00BFFF) to project back.

storyboard.title: The Key-Value Memory Mechanism
lecture_lines: Each hidden neuron acts as a key-value pair.
The first weight matrix stores the "Keys" or patterns.
A "Key" might represent "The capital of France."
The second weight matrix stores the "Values" or facts.
The "Value" vector injects the information "Paris" back.
animations: Display a 'Key' vector (#FFA500) and a 'Value' vector (#EE82EE) side-by-side.
Label Key: 'Pattern: The capital of [Country]' in light orange.
Animate an input vector sliding into the Key, causing it to glow.
Label Value: 'Info: [City Name]' in light violet.
Show the Value vector being released and moving towards the output.

storyboard.title: Step-by-Step: Extracting a Fact
lecture_lines: An input token vector enters the MLP layer.
It is compared against all stored "Key" vectors.
A "Knowledge Neuron" activates when it detects a match.
Non-matching noise is filtered out by activation functions.
The corresponding "Value" vector enriches the token's meaning.
animations: Animate token vector 'Elon Musk' (white) entering the W1 matrix.
Highlight 'Knowledge Neuron #1024' turning bright green (#00FF00).
Show a ReLU graph; a red dot moves up the curve as it activates.
Draw the 'Value' vector (#EE82EE) emerging from Neuron #1024.
Merge 'Elon Musk' and 'Value' vectors into a single 'Enriched' vector.

storyboard.title: Summary and Scaling
lecture_lines: Billions of parameters store millions of these facts.
The Transformer acts as a massive, searchable lookup table.
This "soft" logic allows for flexible knowledge retrieval.
animations: Zoom out to show a grid of millions of pulsing colored dots.
Show multiple query vectors (white lines) hitting different dots simultaneously.
Overlay text 'Massive Searchable Lookup Table' in bright white.
